Independent analytic replay of the norm and variance obstructions, endpoint approximation and absolutely summable product remainder; no finite truncation used for the theorem.
correctness.rationale: Strictly positive probabilities on all finite digit cylinders give full support on the compact K_S. The multiplication operator has spectrum equal to the essential range, here the entire image of K_S, and its norm return is the supremum of the phase error there. Strong return is equivalent to L² return of 1 by bounded multiplication and density of bounded functions. Along cuts with g_j=s_{j+1}−s_j→∞, n=b^{s_j} gives integer head and uniformly vanishing tail. With eventually bounded gaps L, for every large m the first s_j with b^{s_j}≥2m satisfies 1/(2b^L)<m/b^{s_j}≤1/2, so a single-digit point gives a positive norm obstruction for any bias. The conditional variance in that digit is 4p_j(1−p_j)sin²(πm/b^{s_j}), giving a positive L² obstruction for an interior limiting bias. For p_j→0 the expected nonnegative tail along b^{s_j} vanishes. For p_j→1, split off the deterministic all-one tail a_j, and approximate q_j a_j by an integer with 1≤q_j≤Q_j and error ≤1/Q_j, where Q_j→∞ and Q_j sup_{i>j}(1−p_i)→0. The expected phase error at q_j b^{s_j} vanishes; these integers tend to infinity, so pass to an increasing subsequence. For p_j=1/(j+1), injective coding and the divergent sum of rare-digit probabilities imply no atoms; the fair law is also non-atomic. In the rare-digit return product let a_h=exp(2πi b^(−h))−1. The sum of |a_h|/(k+h+1) is O(1/k); the error beyond the linear term is O(1/k²) by the absolute product expansion. Dominated convergence for the linear term and 2−2Re of the product give exactly 4 times the sum of sin²(π b^(−h)), positive and finite. Both examples retain the same spectral support, and the fair law has no strong rigidity sequence by the all-large-m bound.
residual_risks: The dichotomy is verified under convergence of p_j only. At endpoint one the constructed sequence may need an increasing subsequence. Non-atomicity is asserted for the two examples, not all endpoint bias sequences.

evidence: Proposition 3.2(iii) characterizes uniform rigidity of a C_0 multiplier by a Dirichlet range. Here full support gives the same norm, whereas strong U-convergence means Fourier coefficients approach 1 for the particular measure. For positional sets having all digits 0,...,b−1 at allowed positions, their set is the (b−1)-fold sum of the binary set. By the triangle inequality for products of phases and containment in the other direction, the two sets have precisely the same uniform Dirichlet condition.

value.rationale: Within a fixed, explicit spectral family, the criterion separates exactly which features are support-dependent and which depend on the measure. The two full-support atomless laws exhibit opposite strong behavior on the same non-uniformly-rigid set, and the rare-digit example quantifies its return with an exact positive coefficient. This gives a motivated boundary and quantitative witness beyond the old topological gap result or abstract existence of some rigidity measure.
residual_risks: This is a classification in a restricted independent-digit family, not a support classification for general spectral measures or arbitrary nonconvergent weights.
